title: Temporary Scheduler
description:
Job Title: Repairs Scheduler (Temporary)
Location: Gloucestershire
Contract Length: 3 Months
Hourly Rate: 16.00

Are you an organised and customer-focused individual looking for a temporary role within the housing sector? Our client is searching for a dynamic Repairs Scheduler to join their dedicated Repairs Team! If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy coordinating schedules, this is the perfect opportunity for you!

About the Role:
As a Repairs Scheduler, you will play a pivotal role in delivering a seamless repairs service. Your responsibilities will include:

- Diary Management: Monitor and adjust daily diaries to maximise productivity and minimise downtime.

Key Responsibilities:

- Raise and manage works orders in the housing system.
- Process supplier invoices for accuracy and timely payment.
- Support the Repairs Support Manager with reporting and KPI measurement.

What We're Looking For:

- Experience in office administration and database management; knowledge of the housing sector is a plus!
- Strong organisational and communication skills to effectively engage with both internal teams and external partners.
- A proactive attitude with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage your own workload.
- NVQ level 3 or GCSE in Maths and English (or equivalent); qualifications in database management or business administration are advantageous.

title: Client Services Administrator
description:
Client Services Associate IFA Administration

Gloucester £27,000 £32,000 Excellent Benefits

Are you an experienced IFA Administrator or Client Services professional looking to join a progressive financial planning business where your work will be genuinely valued?

We are recruiting for a well-established and forward-thinking independent financial advice firm that prides itself on delivering an exceptional service to its clients. You will join a friendly and supportive Client Services team, providing high-quality administrative support to financial advisers and helping ensure every stage of the client journey runs smoothly.

Previous experience working in an IFA support, financial planning administration or wealth management administration role is essential. This is not an entry-level position, and applications without relevant industry experience cannot be considered.

The Role

As a Client Services Associate, you will support a team of advisers with the administration of new and existing business.

You will act as an important link between clients, advisers and product providers, ensuring applications are processed accurately, queries are resolved promptly and client records remain complete and up to date.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing new business applications and associated client documentation
- Chasing providers and monitoring applications through to completion
- Responding professionally to enquiries from clients, advisers and product providers
- Preparing quotations, applications and key information for client meetings
- Completing electronic identity verification and maintaining accurate client data
- Supporting advisers with client cash management and placing trades through provider platforms
- Maintaining client and policy records using Intelligent Office
- Uploading, checking and organising documentation in line with company procedures
- Managing incoming calls, correspondence and documentation
- Taking ownership of assigned tasks and ensuring deadlines are met
- Supporting the wider team in delivering an efficient and consistently high standard of client service
- Handling confidential client information securely and in accordance with regulatory requirements

What We re Looking For

To be considered, you must have:
- Previous experience in an IFA administration, financial planning support or wealth management administration role
- Experience supporting financial advisers and processing financial-services business
- A working understanding of financial products, provider processes and the regulated advice environment
- Excellent organisation and time-management skills
- The ability to manage several cases and competing priorities simultaneously
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- A professional and client-focused approach
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- Confidence using technology and learning new systems
- Five GCSEs at grade C/4 or above, or equivalent, including Maths and English

Previous experience using Intelligent Office would be advantageous, although it is not essential.

What s on Offer?
- Salary of £27,000 £30,000, depending on experience
- Permanent, full-time employment
- A paid day off for your birthday
- Flexible benefits, including options such as private medical insurance
- Group income protection, critical illness and life insurance options
- Electric car scheme
- Casual dress code
- Comprehensive training and ongoing professional development
- A supportive working environment with opportunities to build your knowledge and progress

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced IFA support professional who enjoys being organised, helping clients and working closely with financial advisers.

If you already have relevant IFA or financial planning administration experience and would like to join a welcoming, ambitious business, please apply today.

title: Operations Assistant - Supply Chain & Procurement
description:
Get Inside the Engine Room of an International Business.

Some Operations Assistant roles keep you firmly in the admin lane.

This one gives you a view across the whole operation.

Join Södra Wood, where you'll support the teams responsible for keeping products, suppliers, data and operational processes moving across our GB and Ireland business.

From raising purchase orders and assisting with supplier interactions to working with ERP systems, analysing operational data and helping introduce better digital processes, you'll gain hands-on exposure to how an international operation really works.

If you're organised, analytical and naturally curious about how businesses run - and you want a role where you can learn, contribute and take on increasing responsibility - we'd love to hear from you.

Please note: Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

The Role at a Glance

Operations Assistant
Cirencester Office Park Hybrid Working - 3 Days Office / 2 Days Home
£27,000 - £30,000 + Excellent Benefits
Permanent Full Time

Occasional Travel: GB, Ireland, Sweden & Finland

Reporting to: Operations Manager

Your Background / Skills: Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, ERP Systems, Purchase Orders, Data Analysis, Supplier Management, Compliance, Process Improvement, Organisation, Problem Solving

The Opportunity

As Operations Assistant, your primary focus will be supporting our Inbound Operations team, while also providing support across Outbound and Compliance when required.

It's a varied role.

One day you could be raising purchase orders and liaising with suppliers; another you'll be analysing operational data, correcting product information or supporting compliance activity.

You'll also get involved in identifying and implementing new digital processes as the business continues to evolve.

To do that successfully, you'll develop a detailed understanding of our ERP and Quality Management Systems (QMS) and how they connect with our wider operational processes.

Over time, you'll gain a broad understanding of the operational tasks, systems and challenges involved in keeping our GB and Ireland business running effectively.

What You'll Be Doing

Inbound Operations & Procurement
- Support product management and procurement processes, helping ensure stock is in the right place at the right time.
- Raise purchase orders and liaise with suppliers to achieve successful outcomes.
- Support the correct release of products for sale through our Inbound processes.
- Identify and correct product coding errors.
- Gather, manage and report critical operational data.
- Adapt data and reporting activity as our digitalisation processes develop.
- Support the Quality and Environmental Coordinator with compliance activity.
- Assist with the satisfactory completion of corrective action reports (CARs).
- Contribute to the identification and implementation of improved digital processes.

Outbound & Compliance
- Provide support with day-to-day Outbound and Compliance activities according to workload and business requirements.
- Monitor treatment solution strengths and report variances.
- Monitor treatment fluid stock levels and arrange replenishment orders.
- Step across different operational activities when additional support is needed.

Data, Systems & Improvement
- Develop a strong working knowledge of our ERP and QMS systems.
- Understand how systems, data and operational procedures work together to deliver the required outcomes.
- Gather and report information that helps the Operations team make informed decisions.
- Identify problems, investigate what's causing them and help find practical solutions.
- Support changes and improvements through to implementation.

About You

You don't necessarily need to arrive knowing everything about timber or our operation - full training will be provided.

What we're looking for is someone with strong organisational and analytical ability who enjoys understanding how things work and takes pride in getting the details right.

You'll be comfortable working with systems and data, communicating with different people and adapting when priorities change.

You'll likely bring:
- Some previous experience working with ERP systems.
- Strong analytical skills and confidence working with operational information and data.
- Excellent organisation and attention to detail.
- Good problem-solving skills and the determination to see issues through to resolution.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- The ability to adapt when circumstances or priorities change.
- A proactive approach to identifying where processes could work better.
- The confidence to work with colleagues, suppliers and other external stakeholders.
- An interest in developing a broader understanding of supply chain and business operations.

Who You'll Work With

You'll become part of a wider operational network and regularly interact with colleagues and partners including:
- Operations leadership and Operations Executives.
- GB & Ireland Sales teams.
- GB & Ireland Finance team.
- Suppliers.
- Hauliers and terminals.
- External permitting and certification bodies.

There may also be opportunities for occasional travel across Great Britain, Ireland, Sweden and Finland as part of the role.

What You'll Get

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll receive:
- Company contributory pension scheme.
- Company Health and Dental Plan, where available.
- Permanent Health Insurance.
- Life Assurance.
- Participation in the Group bonus scheme.
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Opportunity to purchase up to an additional 5 days' annual leave.
- Full training to help you succeed in the role.
- Hybrid working - 3 days office / 2 days home.

Why This Role?

This is a particularly good opportunity for someone who wants to build a broader career in operations, supply chain or procurement.

Rather than being confined to one small part of the process, you'll gain exposure to procurement, stock, suppliers, ERP systems, operational data, compliance and digital improvement.

You'll be joining an international organisation where you'll have plenty to learn, but also plenty of opportunity to contribute.

Your Experience / Background / Previous Roles May Include
Operations Assistant, Operations Coordinator, Supply Chain Assistant, Supply Chain Coordinator, Procurement Assistant, Purchasing Assistant, Operations Administrator, Logistics Coordinator, Logistics Assistant, Stock Coordinator, Purchasing Coordinator or Business Operations Assistant.

Apply Now

If you're organised, analytical and keen to build your career in a role that gives you genuine exposure across an international operation, we'd love to hear from you.

Bring your eye for detail, your problem-solving mindset and your willingness to learn - we'll provide the training and opportunity to develop from there.

Application notice We take your privacy seriously. When you apply, we shall process your details and pass your application to our client for review for this vacancy only. As you might expect you may be contacted by email, text or telephone. Your data is processed on the basis of our legitimate interests in fulfilling the recruitment process. Please refer to our Data Privacy Policy & Notice on our website for further details.

title: Pricing & Contracts Administrator - Excellent benefits + Flexible Working!
description:
Our client based in Quedgeley is a national business with staff geographically spread across the UK and Northern Ireland. They are currently seeking a permanent Pricing & Contracts Administrator to join their growing and dynamic team. The company have a great ethos and are steered towards their core values that promote integrity, collaboration, innovation, and excellence in everything they do!

In this role, you'll manage pricing across company contracts to help protect and improve profit. This includes making sure price increases are applied on time and identifying underpriced contracts so they can be reviewed and updated. The role helps fix past pricing issues, prevent lost revenue, keep up with inflation, and ensure more consistent pricing across all contracts.

The ideal candidate will have strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to understand contract terms and pricing. Comfortable managing data and reports (e.g. Excel), staying organised, and handling multiple deadlines.

Responsibilities:

-Manage and apply contract price increases in line with agreed inflation measures, internal strategy, and contractual terms.

-Identify upcoming price uplifts in advance and ensure they are prepared and implemented on time.

-Work with internal teams to make sure pricing updates are correctly recorded and shared where needed.

-Review contracts to identify underpriced agreements, margin erosion, and outdated pricing structures.

-Analyse pricing data to highlight risks and opportunities, supporting informed commercial decisions.

-Support the Sales team in renegotiating underpriced contracts by providing pricing rationale,

-Create and maintain a central pricing tracker covering contract details, key dates, pricing changes, and status updates.

-Record customer feedback, objections, and negotiation progress within the tracker.

-Ensure the tracker remains accurate, up to date, and used as the single source of truth.

-Produce regular reports on pricing activity, including progress, delays, risks, and key issues.

-Highlight common customer objections and trends to inform future pricing strategies.

-Support regional and local customer accounts with pricing analysis and insight.

-Provide additional pricing support to national accounts when required.

-Act as a central point of coordination between Sales, Operations, and other teams on pricing matters.

-Any other ad-hoc duties as required

Flexible Working -

Monday - Friday, 40 hours per week (flexible start and finish time) - one day per week WFH

Salary - £26,509 + attractive benefits package + free onsite parking

title: Sales Administrator
description:
Sales Administrator

Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire

£30,000 Per Annum + Excellent Benefits! (See Below)

We at JKR are recruiting an enthusiastic individual, for one of our key clients, a growing manufacturing company in Tewkesbury!

Sales Administrator Main Purpose and Scope of Role:

The Sales Administrator is a newly created role at the heart of our client's order-to-delivery process, providing the administrative backbone that allows the Account Management team to focus on customer relationships and account growth.

Working within the Commercial team, the Sales Administrator is responsible for the accurate and timely processing of all customer orders, the maintenance of order data across internal systems (including the company's order-loading system and Salesforce CRM), and the coordination of information between Sales, Supply Chain, and Production to ensure commitments are consistently met.

This is a high-volume, fast-paced role that demands exceptional accuracy, strong organisational skills, and a proactive approach to communication. It also offers a genuine, structured development pathway into Account Management for the right individual who demonstrates the commercial and relationship skills required to progress.

Sales Administrator Main Duties:
- Process incoming customer orders accurately and promptly onto internal systems, ensuring all order details, quantities, pricing, and commercial terms are correctly captured and verified before confirmation
- Enter and maintain sales order information across the company's order-loading system and Salesforce CRM, maintaining data integrity and audit trails for all orders, amendments, and cancellations
- Ensure Supply Chain and Production always have clear, accurate, and timely visibility of material requirements arising from confirmed customer orders, communicating any changes or priority shifts promptly
- Support Account Managers with internal order status queries and coordination activity, ensuring a smooth and well-documented handover of orders from quotation through to fulfilment
- Identify and flag discrepancies, including pricing errors, stock shortfalls, lead time risks, and delivery threats, escalating promptly to the relevant Account Manager or Supply Chain contact with sufficient detail for a timely resolution
- Maintain accurate, auditable records of all order activity, including amendments, cancellations, delivery confirmations, and customer correspondence related to order administration
- Produce regular order status and administrative reports for the Sales, Operations, and Supply Chain teams, highlighting any open issues, overdue actions, or at-risk orders
- Liaise proactively with internal departments including Production, Planning, Quality, and Supply Chain to chase order updates, resolve administrative queries, and ensure customers receive accurate delivery information
- Support the Account Management team during peak periods with quotation administration, customer communications, and general commercial support tasks as directed
- Comply with all Company Health and Safety procedures and contribute to maintaining a safe, organised, and compliant working environment

Sales Administrator Person Specification:
- Sales order processing and administration within a manufacturing, engineering, or technical environment
- Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel at intermediate level or above (data entry, order tracking, reporting)
- Supply chain and production coordination: understanding of how orders translate into material and capacity requirements
- Commercial awareness: pricing structures, order terms, and the importance of accuracy in high-value, technically complex orders
- Proven ability to handle high-volume, fast-paced data entry and order management with a very high level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Experience using a CRM, ERP, or MRP system
- GCSE Maths and English (Grade C / 4 or above) or equivalent - essential for order accuracy and reporting

title: Procurement Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Procurement and Materials Coordinator

Duration: 6 months (extension likely)

Pay rate: Negotiable on experience

Location: Bristol (on site)

Role Summary:

Support the Procurement and Material Control function to ensure the availability of all parts required for the build of various complex systems in a low-volume manufacturing environment.

Key Activities:
- Action RFQs and POs from purchasing BOMs and requisitions to ensure components are available for system builds to meet demanding delivery schedules across both R&D and production.
- Process quotes received and support vendor selection based on price, delivery, and quality, enabling timely customer product delivery. Expedite materials and manage order changes, escalating where necessary.
- Support goods-in, quality control, and stock management processes ensuring all material transactions are recorded in the MRP system. Work with the engineering and production build teams to ensure material handover is clear and flexible according to project needs.
- Provide timely progress and status reports to the Procurement Lead.
- Develop and maintain positive, respected relationships with engineering, procurement, build, and customer teams.

Essential responsibilities:
- Generate POs and follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery.
- Support goods-in, stock control, and kitting functions - monitor inventory and maintain accurate system transactions for all stock movements.
- Ensure batch and serial traceability requirements are met across purchasing, receiving, and inventory transactions.
- Report any delays or deviations in a timely manner to the procurement and engineering teams.
- Support other business functions according to business needs.
- Maintain accurate records of procurement activities - POs raised, deliveries received, using existing software and database tools.
- Support general procurement and material control administration as required.

Qualifications / Requirements:
- 3-5 years' experience in purchasing, planning, or materials roles within a manufacturing environment.
- Hands-on experience with ERP/MRP systems.
- Working knowledge of batch and serial traceability processes and documentation.
- Able to read engineering drawings and understand manufacturing processes.
- Willing to take on a variety of tasks according to business needs.
- Proficient in Excel.
- Strong communication and supplier relationship management skills.
- Enthusiastic about supporting business needs and helping the team achieve goals in a dynamic environment.

Desired characteristics:
- Experience with ERP/MRP systems
- Materials Control experience in a manufacturing environment
- Strong Communication skills (written and oral)
- Highly organised with strong attention to detail and a disciplined approach to transactional accuracy.
- Proactive and responsive, with the ability to manage priorities and follow through on actions in a fast-moving environment.
- Strong problem-solving mindset, with the confidence to identify issues early and escalate where appropriate.
- Able to work effectively across cross-functional teams, building positive relationships with engineering, procurement, quality, and production colleagues.
- Reliable and adaptable, with a willingness to support a broad range of tasks according to business needs.
- Committed to maintaining high standards of record keeping, compliance, and batch/serial traceability.
- Customer-focused, with an understanding of the importance of delivery performance, quality, and clear communication.
